about.tagline: Bharatiya Tatrakshak — the Nation's maritime sentinel
about.mission: To protect our ocean and offshore wealth including oil, fish and minerals. To assist mariners in distress and safeguard life and property at sea. To enforce maritime laws with respect to sea, poaching, smuggling and narcotics. To preserve marine environment and ecology and protect rare species. To collect scientific data and back-up the navy during war.
about.description: The Indian Coast Guard (ICG) is a maritime armed force of the Union operating under the Ministry of Defence. Mandated to protect India's maritime and other national interests across territorial waters, the contiguous zone, and the exclusive economic zone, the ICG works in close coordination with the Indian Navy, Customs, fisheries authorities, coastal police, and international coast guard agencies.

missions.title: Offshore & Installation Protection
missions.description: Ensuring the safety and protection of artificial islands, offshore terminals, installations, and other structures in India's maritime zones.

missions.title: Search & Rescue
missions.description: Providing protection and assistance to fishermen and mariners at sea while in distress — serving as the National Maritime SAR Coordinating Authority.

missions.title: Marine Environment Protection
missions.description: Preserving and protecting the marine ecology and environment, including pollution control and response to oil spills and maritime disasters.

missions.title: Maritime Law Enforcement
missions.description: Assisting Customs and other authorities in anti-smuggling operations and enforcing enactments in force across India's maritime zones.

missions.title: Coastal Security
missions.description: Coordinating coastal security between central and state agencies as Lead Intelligence Agency for coastal and sea borders.

missions.title: National Defence Support
missions.description: Collecting scientific data and, during hostilities, operating under the operational control of the Indian Navy to safeguard national interests.

history.title: Origins — A Need for a Dedicated Force
history.description: Since the 1960s, the Indian Navy advocated for an auxiliary service for maritime law enforcement. Sea-borne smuggling threatened India's domestic economy, and deploying high-value naval warships for patrol duties was not optimal.

history.title: Nagchaudhuri Committee
history.description: The committee identified the need to patrol India's vast coastline, maintain a registry of offshore fishing vessels, and establish a well-equipped force to intercept vessels engaged in illegal activities.

history.title: Rustamji Committee
history.description: Chaired by Shri KF Rustamji, IPS, the committee strongly recommended setting up a Coast Guard-type organisation for general superintendence and policing of India's sea areas. The discovery of oil at Bombay High further reinforced this need.

history.title: Interim Indian Coast Guard Formed
history.description: On 1 February 1977, the interim Indian Coast Guard came into being with two frigates (IN Ships Kirpan and Kuthar) and five patrol boats transferred from the Navy and Home Ministry — a fleet of just seven ships for surveillance across Indian waters and the EEZ.
history.image_alt: Indian Coast Guard ship at sea

history.title: Coast Guard Act — Formal Establishment
history.description: The Coast Guard Act, 1978 was enacted on 18 August 1978, formally inaugurating the ICG as an independent armed force of the Union. Vice Admiral V. A. Kamath of the Indian Navy was appointed the founding Director General.

history.title: MV Alondra Rainbow — Anti-Piracy Success
history.description: The ICG achieved a historic operational success by recapturing the hijacked MV Alondra Rainbow at high seas off Kochi — the first successful prosecution of armed pirates in over a century.

history.title: Post-Mumbai Expansion
history.description: Following the 2008 Mumbai terror attacks, the Government initiated a major programme to expand ICG force levels, assets, and infrastructure for enhanced protection and surveillance of Indian waters.

history.title: India at CGGS Tokyo
history.description: India participated in the inaugural Coast Guard Global Summit in Tokyo, joining the global network of coast guard agencies committed to maritime safety, security, and environmental protection.

history.title: Golden Jubilee & CGGS Presidency
history.description: India hosts the 5th Coast Guard Global Summit in Chennai, assuming the CGGS Presidency while celebrating 50 years of the Indian Coast Guard — from seven ships in 1977 to a multi-dimensional maritime force.

leadership.name: Director General Paramesh Sivamani
leadership.title: 26th Director General, Indian Coast Guard
leadership.message: Guided by our motto "Vayam Rakshamah" — "We Protect", Bharatiya Tatrakshak remains steadfast in its commitment to preserving the sovereignty, security, and maritime integrity of Bharat. In an evolving maritime environment marked by emerging challenges and opportunities, the force continues to uphold the highest standards of professionalism, vigilance, and service to the Nation.

golden_jubilee.title: 50 Years of Service to the Nation
golden_jubilee.description: From seven ships patrolling India's waters in 1977 to a modern multi-dimensional force with over 150 surface units and 77 aircraft, the Indian Coast Guard marks its Golden Jubilee in 2027 — celebrated on the world stage as India hosts the 5th Coast Guard Global Summit in Chennai.
